title: Draft: TCP: Follow TCP Stream handling of tail segments
description:
Flows with missing packets are not completely reassembled by the
dialog window. Particularly, one-side only traffic, or missing
ACKs for the reverse direction end with isolated segments which
require a specific handling when the last flow segment is detected.

Fixes #15160

Ping #12855

When this added parameter is set, the call flow uses a `goto` to jump over the entirety of the original function body, and instead use your added section. When it's unset, the `return false;` you added before the new section causes it to be ignored.

In other words, you've created a useful new function, but hidden it inside the old one behind a confusingly named parameter.

It would be clearer to leave `check_follow_fragments()` alone, and create a new function (perhaps called `unstack_fragments()` based on the label you used for your `goto`) which handles the new functionality.

Yes, absolutely, that could be be in another function. I thought some time on this design between : adding an if/else (in this case all the existing code would be indented, being highlighted by the `diff` ), or a stupid `goto`, or a new function.

The end-half of my comment/suggestion on lines 1607-1637 would be:

```suggestion:-3+0
    return true;
```
As per my comment on `check_follow_fragments()`, this would become a call to `unstack_fragments()`.

As per my comment on `check_follow_fragments()`, this would become a call to `unstack_fragments()`.

changed this line in [version 9 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24904/diffs?diff_id=1898518177&start_sha=921a38b69a3aeb9956b5dd8c29af758551451789#ecc33d9ca259b01be33fa710cd6cf581a15d868b_1858_1876)

This allocation of `follow_record` is assigned to in the `fragment_entry` loop below, but never stored anywhere; that is, it's a memory leak. Future uses of `follow_record` in this function are all separate allocations, and are prepended to `follow_info->payload`.

changed this line in [version 9 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24904/diffs?diff_id=1898518177&start_sha=921a38b69a3aeb9956b5dd8c29af758551451789#ecc33d9ca259b01be33fa710cd6cf581a15d868b_1617_1750)

Possible typo, based on comparing to similar code on lines 1702 and 1661?

```suggestion:-0+0
            follow_info->payload = g_list_prepend(follow_info->payload, follow_record);
```

If I'm mistaken and this is the intended code, then this final allocation of `follow_record` is also being assigned to and then discarded, resulting in another memory leak.

changed this line in [version 9 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/24904/diffs?diff_id=1898518177&start_sha=921a38b69a3aeb9956b5dd8c29af758551451789#ecc33d9ca259b01be33fa710cd6cf581a15d868b_1728_1750)

Wireshark successfully follows the TCP stream for the capture file attached to #15160 when this patch is applied, so it seems to be doing its job. (The Direction dropdown in the *Follow TCP Stream* dialog still says that the conversation has only 1460 bytes, but that's possibly a bug in the dialog, rather than something that can be addressed by this code.)

You use some confusing coding practices which I worry will make the fragment reassembly process harder to understand, and thus to maintain. My biggest concern is that the addition to `check_follow_fragments()` walks and talks like a distinct function, so I believe it should be written as such.
OK David, I'll come back with more compliance to your suggestions. The initial code was itself not the easiest to read, so I thought I was compliant to it :)
